CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for ongoing management of anxiety, evaluation of sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache management.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the current treatment plan. He acknowledges a slight reduction in anxiety levels, particularly during the weekends, but notes that work-related stressors continue to exacerbate his symptoms during the weekdays. Mr. Smith describes experiencing difficulty initiating sleep, with an average sleep duration of approximately 4 to 5 hours per night, often accompanied by frequent awakenings. He reports persistent fatigue, which he attributes to both inadequate sleep and ongoing anxiety, and states that he has been experiencing tension-type headaches approximately three times a week, primarily in the afternoons.
Mr. Smith has been adhering to his prescribed regimen of sertraline 50 mg daily and has recently added melatonin 3 mg at bedtime to assist with sleep initiation. However, he expresses concern regarding the efficacy of the current treatment, stating that he still feels overwhelmed by daily responsibilities and is considering alternative therapies.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 50 mg daily 2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith is a 39-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He lives alone and reports a sedentary lifestyle with limited physical activity. He denies tobacco use and consumes alcohol socially, approximately 1-2 drinks per week. He has expressed interest in exploring stress management techniques and improving his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports anxiety and sleep disturbances. No suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Headaches as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious but stable.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline 50 mg daily, consider increasing to 100 mg if no significant improvement by the next visit. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin 3 mg at bedtime; recommend cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) as adjunctive treatment. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue monitoring; consider adding a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) as needed for headache relief. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage regular physical activity and stress management techniques, including mindfulness and relaxation exercises.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2026-11-01 to reassess symptoms and treatment efficacy. Mr. Smith is encouraged to reach out sooner if his symptoms worsen or if he experiences any side effects from medications.
